note: conv runs at 0.97 MAC/cycle aggregated over all 63 instances = 3.0% of the 32-lane vector unit (Saturn VLEN=256/DLEN=128; the kernels vectorize over OC at e32m4 so vlmax=32). DECISIVE DETAIL: MAC/cyc is FLAT in OC -- 1.06 at OC=32, 1.11 at OC=64, 1.01 at OC=80, 0.84 at OC=128, 0.84 at OC=256. If the OC vectorization were actually paying off, MAC/cyc would scale with min(OC,32); instead it is pinned near 1 no matter how much OC parallelism exists. So the inner loop is NOT arithmetic-bound and NOT vector-width-bound: it is bound by per-reduction-index overhead (one scalar input load + broadcast, one 32-byte weight vector load, address math, loop branch per SINGLE vwmacc). By kernel size: K1 0.61 MAC/cyc (1.9%), K3 1.13 (3.5%) -- K1 is worst because it has the fewest MACs per unit of that fixed overhead. A vwmacc at e32m4 is ~8 cycles of DLEN-128 datapath, so even the datapath model predicts 3-4 MAC/cyc; we get 1, i.e. ~3-4x of pure loop overhead.

change: fp16 roofline calibration for linear_f16/lstm_f16 (GEMV family), derived from Saturn RTL (soc/sim/chipyard/generators/saturn) rather than assumed constants
note: Confirmed via RTL: this hw-config (f2_dual_small_norose_tacit_q31_60mhz -> TARGET_CONFIG=SatGemDualSmallTacitMMIOOnlyConfig -> chipyard SatGemDualSmallTacitConfig) instantiates saturn.rocket.WithRocketVectorUnit(vLen=256, dLen=128, VectorParams.refParams), i.e. VLEN=256/DLEN=128 confirmed exactly (not just assumed). COMPUTE PEAK: FPFMAPipe/SegmentedFMAPipe (exu/fp/FPFMAPipe.scala) instantiates nTandemFMA=dLenB/8=2 segmented-FMA units per cycle; for fp16 (FType.H) each 64-bit segment holds 4 lanes, so narrow (pure-fp16-accumulate, vfmacc.vv) throughput = dLen/16 = 8 FMA/cycle = 16 flop/cycle. Widening (vfwmacc, fp32 accumulator) halves this to dLen/32 = 4 FMA/cycle, since the FMA pipe operates at the OUTPUT eew (32b) once widened. This corrects the campaign's prior uncalibrated '32 ops/cyc' fp16 assumption (id 11/606 notes) -- actual narrow-path peak is 16 ops/cyc, i.e. 2x lower than assumed, meaning the previously-reported 5-11% utilization figures are actually ~10-22% of the CORRECT compute roof (still far from saturated). BANDWIDTH: backend/Backend.scala instantiates exactly ONE LoadSequencer (`vls`) and ONE StoreSequencer for the whole core -- confirmed single-ported vector LSU, vMemDataBits=dLen=128b=16B/cycle peak from L1D (rocket/Configs.scala: vMemDataBits = dLen when useL1DCache). The ORIGINAL (pre-opt) linear_f16/lstm_f16 kernels issue TWO independent vle16 streams per K-chunk (input-row/x/h AND weight), both competing for this single port, capping the achievable rate of the OLD kernel structure at dLen/16/2 = 4 MAC/cycle (half of compute peak) if the port were saturated. MEASURED (fresh paired baseline, id1001): vision_fc 0.90 MAC/cyc (11.3% of 8/cyc peak, 22.6% of the old-structure's own 4/cyc bandwidth roof), lstm_l0 0.60 MAC/cyc (7.5%/15.1%). The gap between measured and even the conservative bandwidth roof (achieving only ~15-23% of it) means load-port sharing alone does not fully explain the low utilization; FPFMAPipe is a depth-4 PIPELINED unit (VectorParams.fmaPipeDepth=4, confirmed NOT overridden by refParams/minParams for this config) and the original kernels' single loop-carried accumulator per (m,n)/gate forces each vfmacc to wait on the PREVIOUS one -- a serial dependency chain that a throughput-pipelined FMA unit cannot hide. FMA pipe depth (4) not independently reconfirmed via a load-only/compute-only microbenchmark (time-boxed out); reduction (vfredusum) cost also not independently isolated. CONCLUSION: real, non-trivial headroom exists (measured utilization is far below BOTH roofs), worth optimizing; the roofline numbers above are ESTIMATED from RTL structure, not from a dedicated microbenchmark -- flagged as such in the final report.

So: IF the underlying per-position ACC_SCALE round were exact, fused relu/pool would be free and exact. It is NOT exact for conv2d's own two-stage-Q0.31 reference (id 1101, unrelated to relu/pool) -- CONFIRMED reproduced on the CURRENT tree: kernels/gemmini/gemmini_conv2d_s8_gemmini_tiled_conv.c alone (dronet, isolated) measures max_abs_err=6, cycles=1,860,175 (vs im2col_full_C's exact 11,598,513 -- a 6.2x conv speedup available AT THE COST of max_abs_err=6, not 0). change: USER DIRECTION: fusion is a flagged optimization; replace binary accuracy labels with computed bounds
note: THREE DECISIONS. (1) conv+relu+pool fusion approved as an OPT-IN optimization behind an enable/disable flag, built on the EXISTING fusion pass infrastructure rather than a parallel mechanism -- note those passes currently fire zero times on yolov8n only because they key on ReLU while that model uses SiLU, so the machinery exists and simply is not matching. Motivation: accuracy_class is a claim, and two kernels claimed bit_exact while measuring err=17 in isolation; a computed bound can be checked, a label can only be trusted.
